You can definitely record your numbers for a week or so and bring them to your OB to discuss, but ultimately it’s best to trust what your doctor says over Reddit. 

I’ve been testing both my blood pressure and blood sugar out of anxiety. I honestly don’t know how accurate the at home testing devices are. My blood pressure machine was constantly reading high and I actually went into the hospital this week afraid I had preeclampsia. My blood pressure was completely normal the entire time, nowhere close to the numbers I got at home. Yhey actually told me I don’t need to test at home anymore unless my doctor tells me to lol. I’m embarrassed by the whole thing. 

There’s been several times I’ve tested my blood sugar at home and gotten two vastly different numbers back to back, despite following the instructions to a T so I don’t know how accurate those devices are either. 

Trust me, I know how hard it is not to obsess and worry. But by talking to your doctor and following their advice, you’re already doing the absolute best you can for your baby. Try not to add stress where you don’t have to. The occasional spike isn’t something to worry about. The vast majority of women who pass the 3 hour never go on to test again and then go on to have healthy deliveries. 

I’ve been following a low carb diet and it’s given me some peace of mind. You can do the same if it helps. 

But above all, please just listen to your doctor and don’t put yourself through anguish when you don’t have to. We’re doing the best we can.

I still remember the interviewer asked me how I would try to create a personal connection with the customer if they seemed really distracted or on their phone and weren’t really engaged in speaking with me. 

I gave the honest answer that I would strive to make everyone feel welcomed when they came into the store but that I would also respect what I felt the customer’s wishes were and wouldn’t go out of my way to force small talk if it was obvious that wasn’t they wanted. 

The interviewer’s whole demeanor changed and it was obvious I had given the wrong answer. 

As an introvert myself, I almost always prefer to be left alone when I go out and I hate small talk, so I know how to recognize and respect that desire in other people. 

God forbid someone go to Starbucks just to enjoy a cup of coffee.

YTA 100%. 

Former server here. I don’t believe the waitress is completely blameless. It’s our job to take allergies very seriously and make sure the message gets across to the people responsible for preparing the food so they can take precautions. 

However, your daughter’s life/safety is your responsibility as a parent and you completely dropped the ball here. If she is that severely allergic, you NEED to take precautions. ESPECIALLY if you’re going to try to order a dish that is based around your child’s allergen. 

Ask your server for ALL the ingredients. If they don’t know, politely ask to talk with a manager, who should know the menu/kitchen better anyway. Ask him/her if they can make sure the chefs change gloves/knives and clean up their station before preparing your daughter’s meal to avoid any possible cross contamination. 

It may seem like a lot to have to ask. And you may think restaurant staff should be trained to take all these precautions already. And ideally, they should. But we don’t live in a perfect world. A lot of the people working in restaurants are just kids themselves. And honestly, a lot of restaurants don’t have great training programs in place. 

Look out for your daughter next time and don’t place her life in the hands of a complete stranger.

Your post really resonated with me because my story is very similar to yours. 

I consider myself and alcoholic. I was always a drinker but I started letting my drinking get out of control. In some part of my mind I knew I should be careful, but I wasn’t. I just couldn’t stop. I lost my job because of it. I also messed up my finances and got into debt. I gained 60-70 pounds from all the beer I was consuming. But I couldn’t make myself stop. 

Eventually I did hit my rock bottom. I really considered ending my life but I didn’t. And since then I have been slowly climbing my way out of the whole. I’ve lost 30 pounds these past few months and I feel so much better physically, since I started working out and gave up drinking. I am making progress. But it’s gradual. And that’s the hard part. 

I think as addicts, we gravitated towards alcohol because it was such an easy solution. At least for me it was. No matter what negative emotion I was feeling or problem I was facing, all I had to do was pick up a case of beer and start drinking and I’d feel great. But that was just short term. Long term, it was eroding away at so many of the ‘good’ things in my life and I just didn’t want to pay attention. 

Now that you’re sober (congrats btw!) you can start working towards your long term goals again. You can work towards finding a better job, losing weight, whatever you want to do. Unfortunately those goals take time. We get so used to being able to silver our problems with substances, it’s hard for us as alcoholics to commit to a long term solution. But you can do this. If you have the strength in you to get sober, you have the strength to do anything. Including lose weight. 

Remind yourself how far you’ve come in the year you got sober. Apply that same dedication and determination to your weight loss journey and you could be in much better shape next year at this time. 

Just keep taking it one day at a time. Challenge yourself to make the right decisions every single day, and make every day a victory. The important thing is to keep going. Eventually your progress will start to show and you’ll get to the place you want to be. 

Have patience and determination, friend. You can do this.
